open_points.subject: M02 Slot.slot_id vs authoring new contract versions
open_points.text: "slot_id: a stable name the creating agent chooses; unique in the kernel, and a name already taken is refused;"
open_points.question: Is a request that names an existing slot_id for a later contract version valid, or must any already-taken slot_id be refused?
options: Only first use of a new slot_id is checked for uniqueness; later contract versions under that slot_id are allowed
Any request naming an existing slot_id is refused, which would block later versions
open_points.default_guess: Only creation of a new slot checks uniqueness; later versions for the existing slot_id are allowed.

open_points.subject: M10 ManifestOperation identity
open_points.text: "Identity evidence: Substitution: equal readings of the same record digest are the same." + candidate fields include "base_url", "required_headers", "instance_class"
open_points.question: If the operation record digest is unchanged but installation-selected instance facts (base_url/headers/class) differ, is that the same ManifestOperation value or a different one?
options: Identity is by operation record digest only; instance facts are runtime context, not identity facts
Identity includes instance facts too; same digest with different instance facts is a different value
open_points.default_guess: Treat instance facts as part of the ManifestOperation value; changed instance facts produce a different value.

open_points.subject: M28 Installation change application
open_points.text: "the configuration is read at start; the token list is read again whenever it has changed"
open_points.question: Are non-token configuration changes (manifest_location/revision, service_instances, credentials, listen address) applied live, or only after restart?
options: Only token-list changes are live; all other config changes require restart
All configuration keys may be reloaded live
Some non-token keys reload live and others require restart
open_points.default_guess: Only token-list changes are live; all other configuration changes require restart.

open_points.subject: map_index semantics across waiting/execution/approval/attempt models (M20, M23, M24, M26)
open_points.text: Candidate fields include "map_index" but do not state its rule for nodes not mapped over a `many` input.
open_points.question: For a node execution/wait/approval/attempt of a non-mapped node, what is map_index?
options: map_index is absent for non-mapped nodes and present only for mapped elements
map_index is always present, using a sentinel such as 0 for non-mapped nodes
open_points.default_guess: map_index is absent for non-mapped nodes and present only when the node is mapped.
